findings: src/main/java/demo/AuthClient.java is the only source file in the repo; it has no build file (no pom.xml/build.gradle) and no existing config/env-var loading mechanism.
The 30s timeout is hardcoded at AuthClient.java:14 via `.timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30))` on the HttpRequest builder passed to refreshToken().
There is no config/properties file, dependency injection framework, or existing pattern in the repo for reading configuration (e.g., env vars or system properties) to model the change after.
No test files exist in the repo, so there's no existing test harness to extend for this change.
risks: Assumption: 'auth timeout' refers to the HTTP request timeout on the token refresh call in AuthClient.java:14, since that's the only timeout in the codebase and the task mentions login/auth timing out.

Assumption: since there's no build file or DI framework in this minimal repo, the simplest and most consistent approach is a constructor parameter with a sensible default, optionally overridable via an environment variable (e.g., AUTH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS), rather than introducing a new config framework.

Since HttpClient itself is constructed once with defaults (HttpClient.newHttpClient()), only the per-request timeout is affected; connection-level timeouts are unaffected unless also made configurable — worth confirming this is sufficient.
No tests exist to validate the change; without a build file it's unclear how this project is compiled/run, so verification may be limited to manual inspection or a quick javac/manual harness.

Changing the default value (if any) away from 30s could alter behavior in production if callers relied on the implicit 30s timeout; plan keeps 30s as the default to avoid behavior change unless overridden.
steps: In AuthClient.java, add a `timeout` field of type Duration, defaulting to Duration.ofSeconds(30) to preserve current behavior.

Add a constructor that accepts a Duration timeout (and keep/add a no-arg constructor that falls back to the default, optionally reading an override from an environment variable such as AUTH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS via System.getenv()).
Replace the hardcoded `.timeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30))` at line 14 with `.timeout(this.timeout)` so the configured value is used when building the request.

If an environment-variable override is desired, parse AUTH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (or similar) once in the constructor, falling back to the 30s default when unset or invalid, and document the variable name in a code comment or README note.

Verify by compiling AuthClient.java (e.g., with javac, since no pom.xml/build.gradle exists) and, if feasible, writing a small manual test/main method to confirm the configured timeout is applied to the built HttpRequest.
input.understanding: The user reports that login (an OAuth token refresh call to the auth server) fails/times out after a fixed 30-second window on staging, and wants the timeout value to be configurable instead of hardcoded, so it can be tuned per environment (e.g., increased for staging) without code changes.
